speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand your infant is experiencing bilious vomiting, an inability to pass meconium, and abdominal distension. To confirm the diagnosis, I need to know if the baby has passed any stool or gas since birth, and has there been any family history of Hirschsprung's disease or intestinal atresia?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia. The clinical presentation of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium, and abdominal distension in a newborn with Down syndrome or polyhydramnios history is highly suggestive of duodenal atresia, often presenting with a "double bubble" sign on imaging. I have already requested a Chest_X-Ray to confirm the double bubble sign.
